scope: Migrated: all 18 packages/* packages (cli, orm, language, sdk, schema, server, zod, common-helpers, testtools, create-zenstack, config/tsdown-config, ide/vscode, auth-adapters/better-auth, plugins/{policy,soft-delete}, clients/{client-helpers,fetch-client,tanstack-query}) — build + lint as cached tasks, test (11 pkgs) as cache:false tasks with dependsOn:['build'], langium codegen as a dedicated generate task. Root package.json scripts (build/watch/lint/test/test:{pg,mysql,sqlite}) now orchestrate via `vp run --filter './packages/**'` (tree model; nested vp run expands in-process — `pnpm build` and `vp run build` both verified). Langium chain modeled BOTH ways as requested: (A) single `&&` chain — vp's item-splitting makes the two codegen steps perpetual cache misses because `langium generate` reads-and-writes src/generated/grammar.ts and the AST patch reads-and-writes ast.ts (warm caps at 5/7=71%); (A') chain + `!src/generated/**` exclusions — 7/7 warm but DEMONSTRABLY incorrect: input config is shared across && items, so after an inert grammar regex edit the patch item's cache hit restored a stale archive over the fresh codegen (grammar.ts on disk had the old regex; --no-cache control produced the new one); (B, chosen) separate `generate` task fusing codegen+patch into one `sh -c` cache unit (exclusions safe because the rw-overlap is internal) + build dependsOn generate — 100% warm, correct invalidation, archive restore. Verdict: separate task + dependsOn fits read-write codegen chains; && items fit write-only step chains (kept for `tsc --noEmit && tsdown` everywhere). Skipped: samples/* (5 pkgs; need zen db push + seed + dev DBs) and tests/* (4 pkgs; e2e/regression/bun/edge need DB matrix and bun) — turbo.json + turbo devDep kept for those subtrees (coexistence; documented caveat that turbo ^build no longer builds packages/* first). pg/mysql test execution skipped (no live DBs); env passthrough they need was verified by probe. CI workflows untouched (noted: they call root scripts, so runners would need vp installed). Inherited partial work was largely kept (18 vite.config.ts files + script stripping were sound); fixed: invalid untrackedEnv-with-cache:false additions, broken vscode:publish/package scripts referencing deleted build script, leftover generator script removed, 2 unformatted files, missing root orchestration, zero verification.
verification: From repo root, vp 0.1.24/node 24: (1) `vp cache clean` then build ×2: cold 0/43 units, 21.7s wall (66s CPU) → warm 43/43 (100%), 0.79s, '40.96s saved'. (2) lint ×2: cold 0/17, 6.0s → warm 17/17 (100%), 0.5s. (3) Selective invalidation: comment edit packages/server/src/types.ts → 41/43 hits (only server's tsc+tsdown items re-ran); comment edit packages/common-helpers/src/index.ts (deepest dep) → only its own 2 items missed, ZERO dependent rebuilds (dependents read its emitted .d.mts which was byte-identical — content-based cutoff beats turbo's hash cascade). (4) Output restore: rm -rf of 3 dist dirs (orm, language, tanstack-query incl. dist/svelte) → 43/43 hits, all restored from archives. (5) Langium chain: grammar comment edit → 5/6 (only generate missed, '--last-details: zmodel.langium modified'), build stayed cached (regenerated files byte-identical); rm -rf src/generated syntaxes → 6/6 hits + files restored; revert edit → miss again (single cache slot confirmed). (6) Design A measured: warm 5/7 with two 'Not cached: read and wrote src/generated/{grammar,ast}.ts'; Design A' stale-restore bug demonstrated with /\s+/→/[\s]+/ probe + --no-cache control. (7) Test suite (sqlite default) via vp: 36 units, 29 build hits restored first, 10/11 test packages green; @zenstackhq/server#test fails with 3/336 pre-existing failures reproduced identically running vitest directly without vp (field-type + openapi baseline drift at this commit). (8) Env probes: TEST_DB_PROVIDER=postgresql reached a cache:false task (PROBE=postgresql) and was stripped from a cached task (UNSET); --no-cache also passes full env. (9) Watch fleet: --parallel started all watchers concurrently (no topo deadlock); kill -INT to vp pid cleaned tsdown watchers but orphaned the run-p subtree. (10) -t '@zenstackhq/orm#build' pulled workspace deps topologically (9/9); cwd-based `vp run build` from packages/ide/vscode worked (3/3); --filter dir-glob with '**' worked for the nested layout. (11) Final `pnpm build` + `pnpm lint` both 100% warm; prettier --check green on all new files.
missingFeatures: Selective env passthrough for uncached tasks: turbo `globalPassThroughEnv: ["TEST_DB_PROVIDER"]` + `test.cache: false` has no precise equivalent — env/untrackedEnv are enabled-cache-config fields and are a load error with cache:false. It only works here because cache:false tasks inherit the FULL environment (no allowlist at all), i.e. zenstack's DB-matrix tests run but with zero env hygiene.

Per-item input/output config for `&&` command items: the langium chain needs '!src/generated/**' for the codegen items but NOT for the patch item's fingerprint; sharing one input config across items forces the sh -c fusion + task-split workaround (and naive exclusions cause silent stale-archive restores).
Watch mode: root `watch: turbo run watch build` (rebuild dependents on change) is approximated by build-once + `vp run --parallel ... watch`; no dependency-aware rebuild.

--continue / no-fail-fast: the 3 pre-existing @zenstackhq/server test failures fast-fail the whole test fleet (3 sibling test tasks cancelled); turbo run test --continue semantics unavailable for CI triage.
Remote/shared cache: build-test.yml matrix (3 DB providers x node versions) re-builds everything per job without a persisted node_modules/.vite/task-cache.

Duplicate package names: root and packages/ide/vscode are both named 'zenstack-v3' (works under pnpm+turbo); `vp run -t 'zenstack-v3#build'` errors 'Package name is ambiguous'. Workarounds verified: cwd-based run or --filter './packages/ide/vscode'.

Single cache slot per task: grammar edit→revert missed on the revert (turbo's content-addressed store would hit); also means the sqlite/pg/mysql matrix would evict each other's entries if tests were ever made cacheable with env fingerprinting.
bugs: cache:false combined with env/untrackedEnv/input/output fails the ENTIRE workspace task-graph load with cryptic 'data did not match any variant of untagged enum UserTaskDefinition' — only names the package dir, not the offending field; should be a targeted diagnostic.

Silent stale-output restore across `&&` items of one task: when an earlier item rewrites files that a later item's archive contains, and those files are input-excluded, the later item cache-hits and restores STALE files over the earlier item's fresh output (demonstrated: grammar regex change present with --no-cache, absent after cached run). vp could detect intra-task write/restore conflicts.

kill -INT to the vp process cleaned up direct child watchers (tsdown --watch) but orphaned the nested process tree of @zenstackhq/tanstack-query#watch (run-p + svelte-package --watch + tsc -w kept running and had to be killed manually).
`vp --version` reports 'vp v0.0.0' despite being the 0.1.24 release (mise-pinned) — breaks version-gated tooling/repro reports.

Minor: first build after running the test pipeline showed 2 transient misses (settled to 43/43 on the next run) — likely vitest-touched files feeding the test-generate items' fingerprints; benign but makes 'second run = 100%' claims order-sensitive.
docsImprovements: Document that the strict env allowlist applies ONLY to cached tasks: cache:false tasks (and --no-cache runs) inherit the full parent environment. This is both the turbo-globalPassThroughEnv migration answer and a security-relevant surprise; current docs imply the allowlist is unconditional.
Document that env/untrackedEnv/input/output are fields of the enabled-cache config and are invalid alongside cache:false; show the failure mode and the correct uncached-task pattern.

Add a codegen-chain cookbook entry (langium/protobuf/graphql-style generate→patch→compile): why `&&` items never cache read-write codegen, why input exclusions on a multi-item task cause stale restores, and the recommended pattern (fuse rw steps with sh -c into one task, declare generated dirs as output + input negations, dependsOn from build).
State explicitly that input negations apply to ALL `&&` items of a task (shared input config), and that each item is a separate cache entry.
Document duplicate-package-name behavior (ambiguity error for -t/name selection) and the cwd/dir-filter workarounds; note pnpm/turbo tolerate duplicates so monorepos like zenstack hit this.
Document that --filter dir-globs support '**' for nested package layouts (./packages/** matched packages/clients/* etc.) — only single-star examples exist in current material.

Document watch-fleet lifecycle: --parallel requirement (topo deadlock otherwise) and that signalling vp does not reliably kill nested process trees (npm-run-all children orphaned); recommend foreground ctrl-c.
Clarify that cwd-based `vp run <task>` from inside a package selects that package only and does NOT pull workspace deps' tasks (unlike -t).
inputExclusionsNeeded: '!dist/**' on every build task (17 packages): tsdown re-reads its previously emitted dist (sourcemaps/bin) on warm rebuilds → perpetual rw-overlap miss without it; bonus: with dist out of the fingerprint, rm -rf dist restores from archive instead of rebuilding (verified on 3 packages).
'!.svelte-kit/**' on @zenstackhq/tanstack-query#build: svelte-package keeps a scratch dir it reads and rewrites.

'!src/generated/**' + '!syntaxes/**' on @zenstackhq/language#generate (the fused sh -c codegen unit): langium generate itself reads-and-writes src/generated/grammar.ts (not just the patch script, which rewrites ast.ts) — both are internal to the unit so exclusion is safe there and ONLY there (same exclusions on the && chain variant cause the stale-restore bug).
surprises: cache:false tasks receive the FULL parent environment — the strict allowlist is cache-only. This flips the playbook's unqualified 'strict env allowlist' claim and made zenstack's TEST_DB_PROVIDER matrix work with zero config (verified by printenv probes both ways).

langium generate is itself a read-write-overlap offender (reads back its previous src/generated/grammar.ts), so even splitting the patch step out wouldn't make a bare codegen item cacheable — the sh -c fused unit + exclusions is the only fully-cached correct shape.

Concrete stale-codegen-restore demonstrated (not just theorized): inert grammar regex edit /\s+/ → /[\s]+/ left old regex on disk after a 6/7-hit run; --no-cache control produced the new regex. Strongest correctness-trap evidence across the migrations so far.

Content-based cutoff outperformed turbo twice: grammar comment edit re-ran codegen but build stayed cached (byte-identical output); deepest-dependency source edit rebuilt nothing downstream (.d.mts unchanged) where turbo's hash cascade rebuilds all dependents.
The repo ships two packages named 'zenstack-v3' (root + VS Code extension) — fine under pnpm/turbo, breaks vp name addressing with a clean ambiguity error; cwd and dir-filter selection both work.

Upstream repo has 3 pre-existing @zenstackhq/server test failures at this commit (field-type + openapi baseline), reproduced byte-for-byte outside vp — would have looked like a migration regression without the control run.

The previous agent's generator script and its emitted configs had diverged (script had untrackedEnv, files didn't — and the untrackedEnv version doesn't even load); reviewing inherited work against the actual loader caught it immediately.
43-unit build graph replays in 0.79s warm through two levels of in-process vp run expansion (root script → filtered graph).
